key_insight: A modified endpoint QuIC assay using a thermal shaker can detect prion seeding activity much faster and more robustly than standard RT-QuIC.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support quicker, more practical laboratory diagnosis of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and improve infection control decisions.
method: Used a ThermoMixer C with vigorous shaking and a single endpoint fluorescence readout.
Minor assay condition changes were made to speed conversion and improve robustness.
Performance was tested on sporadic CJD brain samples and cerebrospinal fluid, including difficult recombinant PrP batches.
evidence_signal: The refined EP-QuIC detected sporadic CJD brain samples within 6 hours, sometimes as early as 2 hours, and showed 100% sensitivity and specificity in CSF in the reported evaluation.
watch_item: Results come from a study evaluation, so broader real-world performance, standardization, and reproducibility across labs still need confirmation.
paper_title: Optimization of a thermal shaker-aided quaking-induced conversion platform for the rapid detection of prion seeding activity in human samples
